answer_1.quote: This is especially evident in tasks such as summarization, dialogue, and creative writing ... we conduct experiments on SummEval (summarization) and Topical-Chat (knowledge‑grounded dialogue).

answer_2.quote: Traditional NLG evaluation metrics like ROUGE and BLEU show clear limitations ... we compare against non‑LLM metrics such as ROUGE-L, BERTScore, MOVERScore, BARTScore, UniEval and BLEU.

answer_3.quote: We introduce CheckEval, a fine‑grained evaluation framework leveraging a Boolean QA checklist ... LLM‑as‑a‑Judge can be categorized into pairwise and pointwise evaluation approaches ... CheckEval, G‑Eval and SEEval all use LLMs to assess generated text.
methods: G‑Eval pointwise Likert prompting with chain‑of‑thought

answer_4.quote: Human evaluation remains the gold standard ... We conducted two distinct human evaluation studies to validate our approach: (1) an assessment of our automated checklist generation process, and (2) a direct comparison between LLM and human scores using the CheckEval protocol.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators were given the same checklist questions and asked to answer yes/no for each criterion; they also rated summaries and dialogue responses on the predefined dimensions.
